sentences.PQFabric:
The relation between Hybrid Post-Quantum Signatures for Hyperledger Fabric and PQFabric is one of contrast between two different points for integrating post-quantum cryptography (PQC) into Hyperledger Fabric. The paper on Hybrid Post-Quantum Signatures for Hyperledger Fabric lists PQFabric [8] in Table 1 as related work on post-quantum blockchain and Fabric integration, and positions its own application-layer approach against PQFabric's deeper, Fabric-internal modifications.

PQFabric integrates hybrid post-quantum mechanisms directly into Fabric's cryptographic and credential-management stack. It modifies internal components such as the Blockchain Cryptographic Service Provider (BCCSP) and the Membership Service Provider (MSP). The paper also distinguishes PQFabric from the work of Abbas et al. [9], which instead extends the identity-provisioning process by modifying the certificate-generation tool (Cryptogen) to embed post-quantum key material in Fabric credentials. The paper states that its own approach "differs fundamentally" from both, because it operates at the application layer and does not alter Fabric's cryptographic stack.

In this comparison, the paper raises several concerns about PQFabric. Changing Fabric's cryptographic components may affect compatibility, maintainability, and deployment complexity. The paper also notes that PQFabric does not fully address system-level benchmarking, including payload-size sensitivity, resource monitoring, block-size overhead, and statistical validation. At the same time, the paper acknowledges a trade-off: because PQFabric's integration is deeper, the paper's application-layer approach offers a narrower scope of quantum resistance.

sentences.Lechhab Ouadrassi et al. [36] Fabric Con: Lechhab Ouadrassi et al. empirically demonstrated that endorsement policy, block size, and peer count significantly affect Fabric latency and throughput [36], motivating the need to control these parameters when evaluating cryptographic changes.
sentences.Melo et al. [35] Stochastic Petri Net Mo: Melo et al. model Fabric performance using stochastic Petri nets and show that block size, batch timeout, arrival rate, and commit capacity can substantially affect mean response time and throughput [35].
